AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why does compost help the environment? (1 mark)
   A. It creates more rubbish
   B. It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   C. It kills all soil animals
   D. It uses up all the water

2. Which of these is a part of a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A container for water
   B. A scarecrow
   C. A compost heap
   D. A tractor

3. Which of these can be used to keep boiled water hot? (1 mark)
   A. A metal spoon
   B. A hot stone
   C. A thermos flask
   D. An open basin

4. Which action wastes fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Using a lid
   B. Using dry wood
   C. Boiling water with no lid and a big flame
   D. Turning the flame down after boiling starts

5. Which of these is a small wild animal that can destroy crops? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Cow
   C. Goat
   D. Weaver bird

6. What might a hungry hare eat in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Stones
   B. Glass
   C. Metal
   D. Young shoots of vegetables

7. Which is a way of conserving wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Setting fires in the bush
   B. Protecting their homes such as forests
   C. Cutting down all trees
   D. Selling them

8. Why do we use more than one method of scaring animals? (1 mark)
   A. It confuses farmers
   B. It uses more soil
   C. Animals can get used to one method
   D. One method is always cheaper

9. Why are weeds removed from the seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. They take water, light and food from the crop
   B. They protect seedlings from rain
   C. They are colourful
   D. They add manure

10. Why should a container seedbed have holes at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. Insects can leave
   B. Seeds can escape
   C. To make it lighter
   D. Extra water can drain out

11. What is transplanting? (1 mark)
   A. Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   B. Sowing seeds directly
   C. Making compost
   D. Harvesting

12. Why should fruit be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To change its colour
   B. To remove dirt and germs
   C. To make it dry
   D. To make it sour

13. Which is likely to take longest to give fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Passion fruit
   B. Mango tree
   C. Radish
   D. Pawpaw

14. What is topsoil? (1 mark)
   A. A fertiliser
   B. The bottom layer
   C. Sand from the river
   D. The dark top layer of soil

15. What is a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. A tool for cutting
   B. A support structure for climbing plants
   C. A type of fruit
   D. A bag for seeds

16. Where should you buy fruit seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. A trusted nursery or agrovet
   B. From a scrap yard
   C. From anyone on the road
   D. From a stream

17. Which of these can oxen do on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. Give wool
   B. Pull ploughs and carts
   C. Lay eggs
   D. Produce honey

18. What is the purpose of vaccinating animals? (1 mark)
   A. To prevent diseases
   B. To make them noisy
   C. To make them heavier
   D. To colour them

19. Why do we cook food? (1 mark)
   A. To make it dirty
   B. To make it disappear
   C. To make it colder
   D. To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat

20. How do you test if boiled potatoes are cooked? (1 mark)
   A. A fork goes in easily
   B. They are still very hard
   C. They turn green
   D. They float

21. What are germs? (1 mark)
   A. Kinds of soap
   B. Tiny living things that can cause disease
   C. Large animals
   D. Types of food

22. How should drinking water be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a clean container with a lid
   B. In an open basin
   C. With a dirty cup
   D. On the ground

23. Why should fingernails be kept short? (1 mark)
   A. Nails are food
   B. Long nails are heavy
   C. Short nails grow faster
   D. Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails

24. Why should food be covered in the kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. To keep off flies, rats and cockroaches
   B. To hide the plate
   C. To keep it hot forever
   D. To make it heavier

25. Why should stagnant water be emptied from tins and tyres? (1 mark)
   A. Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   B. It is too clean
   C. It smells of soap
   D. It cools the compound

26. Why should cleaning be done in an open place with drainage? (1 mark)
   A. To get wet
   B. So dirty water does not make a puddle
   C. To be seen
   D. To make noise

27. In even tacking, the stitches and gaps are (1 mark)
   A. Different lengths
   B. Absent
   C. The same length
   D. Very long

28. How long should a length of thread be for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. As long as the room
   B. 10 metres
   C. 1 cm
   D. About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm

29. Which tool holds a needle safely on the finger to push it? (1 mark)
   A. Pin cushion
   B. Thimble
   C. Scissors
   D. Ruler

30. What should you never do with a needle? (1 mark)
   A. Thread it
   B. Keep it in a pin cushion
   C. Put it in your mouth
   D. Use a thimble

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Name three PPE items and what each protects. (3 marks)

32. A drip system drips very fast at one hole and not at all at another. Explain what may be wrong and how to fix each. (4 marks)

33. Give two reasons why soil should be conserved. (2 marks)

34. Give three ways of caring for a drip irrigation system. (3 marks)

35. Name three crops established by direct sowing of tiny seeds. (3 marks)

36. Describe how to make a bottle drip for one plant. (3 marks)

37. Name three foods that can be shallow fried. (3 marks)

38. Why should personal items like towels not be shared? (2 marks)

39. Describe the first aid for a small burn. (3 marks)

40. Name three methods of cleaning the home environment. (3 marks)

41. Why should you brush teeth twice a day? (2 marks)

42. Give two reasons why goats are suitable for dry areas. (2 marks)

43. Explain pruning. (2 marks)

44. Give three reasons why PPE should be cleaned. (3 marks)

45. How do fruits help our health? (3 marks)

46. State three safety rules when using needles and scissors. (3 marks)

47. What is meant by coexisting with wild animals? (2 marks)

48. Compare even tacking and long and short tacking. Say which is quicker and which holds more firmly. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   It turns waste into useful manure.

2. A — A container for water
   A container holds water for the pipe or bottle.

3. C — A thermos flask
   A flask keeps water hot so it need not be boiled again.

4. C — Boiling water with no lid and a big flame
   Heat escapes without a lid and a big flame.

5. D — Weaver bird
   Weaver birds and other birds eat grain crops.

6. D — Young shoots of vegetables
   Hares nibble young plants.

7. B — Protecting their homes such as forests
   Protecting habitats lets animals live.

8. C — Animals can get used to one method
   A mix of methods works better.

9. A — They take water, light and food from the crop
   Weeds compete with crops.

10. D — Extra water can drain out
   Waterlogged soil rots seeds and roots.

11. A — Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   Transplanting means moving seedlings.

12. B — To remove dirt and germs
   Clean fruit is safe to eat.

13. B — Mango tree
   Big trees like mango take several years.

14. D — The dark top layer of soil
   Topsoil is rich in plant food.

15. B — A support structure for climbing plants
   A trellis is posts and wires to hold climbers.

16. A — A trusted nursery or agrovet
   Good seedlings are disease-free and true to type.

17. B — Pull ploughs and carts
   Oxen give draught power.

18. A — To prevent diseases
   Vaccination protects animals from diseases.

19. D — To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   Heat kills germs and softens food.

20. A — A fork goes in easily
   Soft potatoes are ready.

21. B — Tiny living things that can cause disease
   Germs cannot be seen without a microscope.

22. A — In a clean container with a lid
   Covering keeps germs out.

23. D — Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
   Clean short nails prevent infection.

24. A — To keep off flies, rats and cockroaches
   Covered food is protected.

25. A — Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   Mosquitoes spread malaria.

26. B — So dirty water does not make a puddle
   Dirty water can breed mosquitoes.

27. C — The same length
   Even tacking is equal.

28. D — About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
   Long thread tangles.

29. B — Thimble
   A thimble protects the finger.

30. C — Put it in your mouth
   Needles are dangerous in the mouth.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: The first hole is too big, so tie cloth around it or use a smaller hole. The other hole is blocked, so clear it gently with a thin wire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cause and fix for both holes.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Soil grows our food, and if it is washed away or made poor the crops will fail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soil grows food, 1 mark for erosion or loss of plant food.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fill the container daily, check for leaks and blocked holes, keep the water covered and clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Carrot, millet, amaranth, radish, sorghum (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each crop.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make tiny holes in the cap, fill the bottle with clean water, bury the neck upside down near the plant, press soil around it and refill when empty.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for holes in cap, 1 mark for placing near plant, 1 mark for filling and refilling.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, fish, sausages, onions, chapati (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Germs and skin infections spread through them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for infection.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the burn under cool running clean water for at least ten minutes, cover it loosely with a clean cloth and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweeping, dusting, mopping and disposal of refuse (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: It removes food and germs that cause decay and keeps the mouth fresh.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for removing food, 1 mark for preventing decay.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: They eat leaves, shrubs and grass, and can live where cattle find little to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is cutting off dead, weak or crossing branches so that light and air can reach the plant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cutting, 1 mark for the purpose.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can carry germs, it may smell or spoil, and clean PPE lasts longer and protects better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins that fight illness, fibre that helps digestion and water that keeps the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never put needles in the mouth; keep them in a pin cushion; count them; carry scissors with points down (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Living together peacefully so that both farmers and animals are safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for living together, 1 mark for both safe.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking is more even and holds more firmly; long and short tacking is quicker because each stitch covers more cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for each stitch description, 1 each for quicker and firmer.
